findings.title: Public `findMany` removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions` (breaking API change)
findings.body: The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method is removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any caller that used `findMany` (for example tRPC handlers) will fail to compile or break at runtime. The diff does not update any other callers, and the PR description does not mention the removal. Callers must now write their own `$queryRaw` and handle the view's column names and typing themselves. Confirm all usages are migrated, or keep a compatibility wrapper.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
findings.body: The "Caching" describe block was removed. The service still has `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, and `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` still rely on that caching. Nothing now verifies that the second call returns the cached value, or that a `null` filter result is cached rather than rebuilt. The tests should have been converted to the Sql format, not dropped.

findings.title: Filter condition returned as an unparenthesized top-level OR
findings.body: For the single-filter case, `getFilterConditions()` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no outer parentheses. `getBaseConditions` wraps it, so that path is safe. Any other caller that embeds the public result as `... AND ${filterConditions}` gets wrong operator precedence, which would silently widen the result set. Wrapping the OR in parentheses where it is built would make the fragment safe to compose.

findings.title: Exact-SQL equality tests are brittle and miss the empty-membership branches
findings.body: The tests assert exact Sql structure and parameter order, including the order of user IDs returned by the membership query, which has no `ORDER BY`. A harmless reformat or a different row order will fail them. The new branches that skip the `userId = ANY(...)` clause when the user list is empty, in both the team and org builders, have no test coverage.
